rows.question: How many people did Apple employ at the end of fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: Approximately 167,000 full-time equivalent employees.
rows.answer: Apple had approximately 167,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 26, 2026 [AAPL-2026-00013].

rows.question: What were Apple's total net sales in fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: $478,834 million, up 15% from 2025.
rows.answer: Apple's total net sales in fiscal 2026 were $478,834 million [AAPL-2026-00112]. This matches the segment total in the MD&A [AAPL-2026-00066] and the geographic total [AAPL-2026-00111].

rows.question: How much is Apple's quarterly dividend per share?
rows.reference_answer: $0.27 per share, which Apple intends to increase annually.
rows.answer: Apple's quarterly cash dividend was $0.27 per share as of September 26, 2026 [AAPL-2026-00071]. The company raised it from $0.26 to $0.27 per share beginning in May 2026 [AAPL-2026-00071].

rows.question: Where is Apple's head office?
rows.reference_answer: Cupertino, California.
rows.answer: Apple's headquarters is located in Cupertino, California [AAPL-2026-00056]. Its principal executive offices are at One Apple Park Way, Cupertino, California 95014 [AAPL-2026-00000].

rows.question: What share of Apple's revenue is sold through resellers and carriers rather than directly?
rows.reference_answer: About 60% of total net sales came through indirect distribution channels.
rows.answer: Approximately 60% of Apple's total net sales in 2026 came through its indirect distribution channels, such as third-party cellular network carriers and other resellers [AAPL-2026-00007]. The remainder is sold directly through its retail and online stores and direct sales force [AAPL-2026-00007].

rows.question: Why is Tesla's reliance on its CEO considered a risk?
rows.reference_answer: Tesla is highly dependent on Elon Musk, who does not devote his full time to Tesla and holds roles at SpaceX, xAI, Neuralink and The Boring Company.
rows.answer:
Tesla describes its dependence on Elon Musk as a risk because he is highly dependent on Musk's services as Technoking and CEO, and Musk does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla [TSLA-2025-00042]. Musk also holds management positions at other companies, including SpaceX, xAI, Neuralink and The Boring Company, and is involved in other ventures [TSLA-2025-00042].

Tesla also flags risks tied to Musk's personal financial position:
- Certain banks have extended credit to Musk secured by pledges of Tesla common stock [TSLA-2025-00061].
- If the stock price declined substantially, Musk could be forced to sell Tesla shares to satisfy loan obligations [TSLA-2025-00061].
- Musk may also need to sell shares to meet commitments to other ventures or tax obligations from the 2018 CEO Performance Award, and such sales could cause the stock price to decline [TSLA-2025-00061].

Tesla further notes that the product goals in the 2025 CEO Performance Award were designed to incentivize Musk, and that investments tied to them may not deliver expected benefits, which could lead to write-downs and harm financial performance and the stock price [TSLA-2025-00061].

rows.question: When did Tesla start its autonomous ride-hailing service?
rows.reference_answer: Tesla launched its Robotaxi service in June 2025.
rows.answer: Tesla launched its Robotaxi autonomous ride-hailing service in June 2025 [TSLA-2025-00032][TSLA-2025-00006].

rows.question: How much battery storage capacity did Tesla deploy in 2025?
rows.reference_answer: 46.7 GWh of energy storage products.
rows.answer: Tesla deployed 46.7 GWh of energy storage products in 2025 [TSLA-2025-00074].

rows.question: What is Tesla's Cybercab?
rows.reference_answer: Tesla's purpose-built autonomous vehicle for its Robotaxi business.
rows.answer: Cybercab is Tesla's purpose-built autonomous vehicle, which will be part of its Robotaxi business over time [TSLA-2025-00006]. Tesla has plans to mass produce Cybercab, a purpose-built Robotaxi product [TSLA-2025-00032]. Tesla's Robotaxi business currently operates with Model Y vehicles, but in time will include Cybercab [TSLA-2025-00006].

rows.question: Which chip architecture generated most of NVIDIA's data center sales?
rows.reference_answer: Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center revenue.
rows.answer: Blackwell architectures represented the majority of NVIDIA's Data Center revenue in fiscal year 2026 [NVDA-2026-00091].

rows.question: How large is NVIDIA's workforce and how much of it is in R&D?
rows.reference_answer: About 42,000 employees in 38 countries; 31,000 in research and development.
rows.answer:
It says more than 80 percent of the workforce have technical roles [NVDA-2026-00026].
More than half of the workforce hold an advanced degree [NVDA-2026-00026].

rows.question: How is the Chinese government affecting NVIDIA's data center business?
rows.reference_answer: China has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged purchases of NVIDIA products, which may hurt Data Center revenue.
rows.answer:
- The Chinese government has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged them from purchasing, importing, or using NVIDIA's data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls [NVDA-2026-00070] [NVDA-2026-00025].
- Increased government oversight of digital platform companies may adversely affect Data Center revenue, even if NVIDIA is able to participate in the China data center compute market [NVDA-2026-00070].
- A Chinese government agency announced an Action Plan endorsing new standards for compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth of accelerators used in new and renovated China data centers [NVDA-2026-00070].
- The Chinese government could modify or implement that Action Plan in a way that effectively prevents NVIDIA from designing products to meet the new standard, which may restrict customers' use of some of its data center products [NVDA-2026-00070].
- As of the end of fiscal 2026, NVIDIA was effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center compute market, and it is unable to deliver a product that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government [NVDA-2026-00023].

rows.question: How much revenue did the iPhone bring Apple in fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: $254,098 million, up 21% from $209,586 million in 2025.
rows.answer: iPhone net sales in fiscal 2026 were $254,098 million [AAPL-2026-00086]. This is also reported as $254,098 million with a 21% change from 2025 [AAPL-2026-00067].

rows.question: How much did Apple spend on research and development in fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: $45,765 million, up 32%, equal to 10% of total net sales.
rows.answer: Apple spent $45,765 million on research and development in fiscal 2026 [AAPL-2026-00069][AAPL-2026-00076].

rows.question: How much of its own stock did Apple buy back in fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: $85.8 billion of common stock (and $15.7 billion paid in dividends).
rows.answer:
Apple repurchased $85.8 billion of its common stock during 2026 [AAPL-2026-00071].
It repurchased 297 million shares for $85.8 billion [AAPL-2026-00104].

rows.question: What were Apple's Services net sales in fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: $123,301 million, up from $109,158 million in 2025.
rows.answer: Apple's Services net sales in fiscal 2026 were $123,301 million [AAPL-2026-00086].

rows.question: Why did Apple's sales in Greater China rise in 2026?
rows.reference_answer: Higher net sales of iPhone and Mac, plus a favorable effect from the stronger renminbi.
rows.answer: Greater China net sales increased in 2026 primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone and Mac [AAPL-2026-00067][AAPL-2026-00066]. The strength in the renminbi relative to the U.S. dollar had a favorable year-over-year impact on Greater China net sales during 2026 [AAPL-2026-00067][AAPL-2026-00066].

rows.question: What was Apple's gross margin percentage on products in 2026?
rows.answer: Apple's products gross margin percentage in 2026 was 39.3% [AAPL-2026-00068].

rows.question: What were Tesla's total revenues in 2025 and how did they change from 2024?
rows.reference_answer: $94,827 million, down 3% ($2,863 million) from $97,690 million in 2024.
rows.answer: Tesla's total revenues were $94.83 billion in 2025 [TSLA-2025-00074]. This was a decrease of $2.86 billion compared to 2024 [TSLA-2025-00074]. The segment table shows total revenues of $94,827 million in 2025 versus $97,690 million in 2024, a decline of $(2,863) million, or (3)% [TSLA-2025-00088].

rows.question: How much revenue did Tesla's energy business generate in 2025?
rows.reference_answer: Energy generation and storage segment revenue was $12,771 million, up 27%.
rows.answer: Tesla's energy generation and storage segment generated revenues of $12,771 million in 2025 [TSLA-2025-00194].

rows.question: What is Tesla's Cortex?
rows.reference_answer: Tesla's AI training cluster at Gigafactory Texas; Tesla is also building Cortex 2.
rows.answer: Cortex is Tesla's training cluster at Gigafactory Texas [TSLA-2025-00009]. In 2025, Tesla further expanded Cortex [TSLA-2025-00009]. Tesla is currently building Cortex 2 at Gigafactory Texas to further increase its AI training compute capacity [TSLA-2025-00009].

rows.question: Which company is Tesla working with to make AI chips in the United States?
rows.reference_answer: Samsung, to manufacture advanced semiconductors for AI inference and training in the U.S.
rows.answer: Tesla announced a new collaboration with Samsung to manufacture advanced semiconductors for AI inference and training in the U.S. [TSLA-2025-00009]

rows.question: What share of Tesla's employees receive stock as part of their pay?
rows.reference_answer: 92% of employees are included in total rewards packages with stock ownership opportunities.
rows.answer: Tesla says 92% of employees are included in total rewards packages, which emphasize stock ownership opportunities [TSLA-2025-00023].

rows.question: What was NVIDIA's total revenue for fiscal year 2026?
rows.reference_answer: $215.9 billion ($215,938 million), up 65% from a year ago.
rows.answer: NVIDIA's total revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $215,938 million, up 65% from a year ago [NVDA-2026-00094]. The consolidated statement of income also reports revenue of $215,938 million for the year ended January 25, 2026 [NVDA-2026-00126].

rows.question: How large was NVIDIA's charge related to the H20 chip and what caused it?
rows.reference_answer: A $4.5 billion charge in Q1 fiscal 2026 for excess H20 inventory and purchase obligations, after new U.S. export licensing requirements.
rows.answer: NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations [NVDA-2026-00064]. The charge was caused by the USG's April 2025 requirement for a license to export H20 integrated circuits to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, as the demand for H20 products diminished [NVDA-2026-00064][NVDA-2026-00092].

rows.question: How much did NVIDIA spend repurchasing its shares in fiscal 2026?
rows.reference_answer: 282 million shares for $40.4 billion.
rows.answer: NVIDIA repurchased 282 million shares of its common stock for $40.4 billion in fiscal year 2026 [NVDA-2026-00087][NVDA-2026-00172].

rows.question: How much H20 revenue did NVIDIA earn under U.S. export licenses?
rows.reference_answer: Approximately $60 million.
rows.answer: NVIDIA generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under the licenses granted in August 2025 [NVDA-2026-00064].

rows.question: When did NVIDIA buy Mellanox and what did it add?
rows.reference_answer: In 2020; it added networking and made NVIDIA's platforms data-center scale.
rows.answer: NVIDIA acquired Mellanox in 2020 [NVDA-2026-00007]. The acquisition expanded NVIDIA's offerings to include networking, enabled its platforms to be data center scale, and led to the introduction of a new processor class, the data processing unit, or DPU [NVDA-2026-00007].
